newsitem.title: FRANCE: POLL - French rightists oppose National Front pact.
newsitem.headline: POLL - French rightists oppose National Front pact.

text.p: A majority of France's mainstream right-wing voters favour a hard-line approach to the sensitive issue of immigration but oppose an alliance with the far-right National Front, according to a poll released on Thursday.

The Sofres poll for the weekly Figaro magazine found that 73 percent of backers of the Gaullist Rally for the Republic (RPR) or the centrist Union for French Democracy (UDF) want the state to take a harder line on the immigration issue.
However, 70 percent said they would oppose a pact between the mainstream right and the anti-immigration National Front led by Jean-Marie Le Pen.

The French Right has been reeling since the previous conservative government, an alliance of the RPR and UDF, was swept from power in a June 1 parliamentary election and replaced by a leftist alliance of Socialists, Communists and Greens.
The election obliged Gaullist President Jacques Chirac to share power with a government led by Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin.
A key reason for the centre-right's defeat was the strong performance of the National Front, which divided the right by drawing nearly 15 percent of the vote in the parliamentary poll.

But the mainstream right has been hesitant to reach out to the Front, which wants to ship home even legal immigrants and favours a national preference in jobs, housing and education for native-born French people.
French Gaullists distanced themselves this week from a senior member of the party who had dinner with Le Pen and later advocated talks with the Front.
The party's National Assembly group described the dinner as a private and regrettable initiative by fellow-deputy Robert Pandraud.
The Sofres poll was based on interviews with 400 individuals who said they had voted for Gaullist President Jacques Chirac in 1995.
